newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Timor students march to governor's office in Dili.
newsitem.headline: Timor students march to governor's office in Dili.

text.p: Several thousand East Timorese demonstrated on Thursday against Indonesian criticism of Nobel peace laureate Bishop Carlos Belo, with crowds marching peacefully to the governor's office in Dili.

"About 5,000 school and university students held a demonstration outside the governor's office, but it was orderly and there were no problems and no violence," East Timor's deputy police chief Colonel Atok Rismanto told Reuters by telephone.
Demonstrators have held daily protests since Tuesday in support of Belo, who is highly respected in mainly Catholic East Timor, a former Portuguese colony.
The bishop has been the focus of protests and media attacks in Jakarta for reportedly saying in a German magazine interview that Indonesian troops treated East Timorese like "dogs".
Rismanto said the protesters presented a petition to a representative of Governor Abilio Soares, who is currently travelling in rural areas. Soares is due back in Dili on Friday.
Rismanto said the crowd had begun to disperse around noon (0400 GMT). Other witnesses said there was no confrontation between the students and security forces.
Residents said students and other demonstrators had gathered in the early morning outside the University of East Timor.

Some protesters carried banners saying "Viva, Bishop Belo". Belo, who is in Jakarta attending an annual conference of Roman Catholic bishops, has refused to comment on the reported remarks carried in the German news magazine Der Spiegel.

The East Timor protests started on Tuesday, the fifth anniversary of the killing of at least 50 protesters by troops in Dili after a funeral for an anti-Indonesian activist. Witnesses and human rights groups estimated at least 180 people died.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in December 1975 and declared the territory its 27th province the following July, a move never recognised by the United Nations.
Police said demonstrators broke some windows at the local legislature on Wednesday before moving on to the governor's seafront office, after which they dispersed peacefully.

A source in close contact with East Timor said the students were still upset over the attacks on Belo, regarded as probably the most influential civilian in East Timor, and people had travelled from outside of Dili to join the protest.
"A numbers of students have come from as far away as Baucau to join the protest in support of Bishop Belo," the source said. Baucau lies 100 km (60 miles) to the east of Dili.
